title: Where the Stroke Stopped

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The stone keeps the place where the broom stopped, and the iron keeps the finger that waits in it. The fire keeps its fifth where nobody has looked for a hundred days. What is kept in three places does not add up to an account.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the Clay Yard, spoken at the last tend of Tallow

where: Low Kiln and the Clay Yard, Sill
pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-seventy-to-one-hundred-and-seventy-two-day-old body carried everywhere, told by nobody; the surgeon's register colours the noticing (the firing as an operating theatre he cannot enter with heat kept and counted behind a screen and a gate of two bites, the carrying arm as a record in muscle that keeps weight and not cost, the fire's unanswered fifth as a chart closed over its finding with the neat margin showing, the near-saying held at the word as a clamp left too long) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, back-room interior, Marra in Sill, tenth stopping, seventh hearing, calling of the loan, spending of the seventh year or ending; the foundling stays offstage, the green is never Fenna in narration, and no name, figure or payer is given to any withholding

scenes.title: The Last Working Week Opens
scenes.synopsis: First entry, first dated heading and drop capital of the chapter: Day 170, Tallow 21, Firstday, before first grey through mid-morning under the Vail kiln-house roof, at the hearth, the kiln mouth, the drying racks and the yard well. The boy is one hundred and seventy days old and five months and twenty days and nobody under any roof says so (T071/T072). The first smell is hot clay under tallow and the first sound is the kiln's breath in fours with a gap, not a bell; the carried fire under the broken pot answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and seventy days (T058/T079, T088). Sella gives every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, says the house where another woman would say I, keeps the half-pace from every open slate, and leaves the widow's mark where it hung, because a morning and a shelf are not openings; she turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, tells the fire it was the thaw, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist and sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, her hand resting a half-beat longer than the setting needed. The crust lies stiff two inches from his ear with its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread of drool frozen and unwiped, his hand outside the wool going up an inch toward the note of water over water and coming down against the fold. The yard goes around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried); the trough stands bare and dark and the water is called weather, the clay jar cold under its glaze is glanced at once and not touched, and the shallow pan's gone place keeps its round ring on a tray of its own. Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late while going on wanting the late because it puts off the paying, sweeps over the collector's road without once turning along it, and no collector comes; six are counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh is held at the lip of the sill where it cannot, the small knife back at the very edge with Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holding what light there is and giving it back, his chest tight since the dark and the warm stone Sella gave him in the winter Garl died cold in the clay pot in the loft, unreconciled by not trying (T036/T076, T006 held). Nine stoppings stay nine objects and not a rule with no payer named to any, the tenth withheld, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled (T061/T082). The Day 161 fraction at the damper and the Day 166 held beat beneath the loaf shelf stand on separate places and are not repeated or joined, and no fourth likeness is made a cause. The danger gathers in the dust ground small as meal on the wrong wind and the sweetish lead edge from High Kiln, with no room changed and no pot lost; a pot set down at the racks gives a high thin note before its time and the woman who set it down does not hear it, and the boy files the sound as a danger and not as a fourth near-full answer. He reads the firing as a theatre he cannot enter --- heat kept and counted behind a screen, a gate of two bites, a cost paid by a man whose name is not spoken --- and the file he turns out is exact and worthless, an inventory that is not a key and a list that is not a hand. Three counts stay in three places: the kiln's breath behind the wall, the river's note of water over water through the finger's-width door as a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings, and the boards' four nails, four and a knot the width of a thumb overhead. The old life stays offstage: no tagged memory and no present-tense break (T004).

scenes.title: The Cost Sent to the Pot
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 170, midday into the going of the light at the yard well, the drying racks, the loaf shelf and under the Vail roof; no new dated heading, the day already opened in Scene 1. A neighbour with a wet pot asks what a firing costs set down in the Vail house; Sella glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze, does not touch it, and sends the woman to the pot with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it, and the woman carries the unanswered question away level so nothing slops and nothing is priced (T077). At the racks the yard goes around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates and the field's empty place where a hand went in on Seed 15, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). Sella moves her lips along her own loaf row standing with two gaps and gives nobody a figure; the two unnamed gaps (the old space at the row's end and the palm's breadth that came in on the night of Seed 6), the one stiff brown-edged crust in the fold and its empty place, the shallow pan's gone place on its own tray and the field's empty place stay in rooms and on trays that do not touch, no third gap comes and no fourth likeness is made a cause (T060/T086, T097). From the basket's low angle the underside of the loaf shelf becomes a roof and the charcoal marks wait under its front edge; Sella does not reach beneath the board this day and the boy does not read, count or copy the marks, which wait for a hand that is not his and a day that has not come (T100 carried, not paid). At the going of the light she carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke going before her and the river wind coming up to meet it, going wide around the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough and the rack space without explaining the turns to the basket; she sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face, leaves the thread frozen and unwiped, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed, tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist and sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, and does not look toward the bed. The widow's mark hangs where it hung and is not touched, because a dusk is not an opening and the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour (T058/T079). The fire answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and seventy days (T088), and the two rooms do not touch. The boy's count stands at one hundred and seventy, exact, complete and unspent, spoken by nobody (T071/T072).

scenes.title: The Finger in the Iron
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, second dated heading: Day 171, Tallow 22, Secondday, before first grey into the morning at the Vail wheel-shed, the flagstones, the cold damper and the drying racks. Three or four men go low into the finger's-width-open back room before first grey and get no name; Sella carries past at the half-pace, turns no head and does not say the room is cold, and the two shut-room tellings stand side by side with no third (T065/T095). Jorra comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger and under the nails, not bone-coloured slip, asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, and keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray while the broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack, entered by nobody (T035/T031). He speaks to the wheel before anyone (It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady), tells a pot You'll do, knows its full note before it leaves the wheel and withholds the knowing from a High Kiln kiln-master who comes up on the wrong wind and says a pot singing before its time generally sings itself out early; the knowing goes to the near-full tray, beside the hearings and never among them, advanced and not paid, and no pot is lost in the yard (T061/T082). **The chapter's one meaningful change:** when Sella's instruction is low and unfinished (The fire's low. It wants---), Jorra's bent finger goes to the cold iron of the damper and stops, as on Tallow 12 and Tallow 15; he holds the iron while she finishes It wants feeding, then moves the tongue a hair's breadth and leaves it standing. The fraction at the iron is remembered in the holding and not in a word, nobody speaks of the waiting and no payer is named (T062). This time, while the finger still stands in the iron and the sentence has finished, Tarn, come up the yard with the broom, checks his stroke for half a beat behind the standing finger on the flagstones and then goes on toward the road without a word or a turn of the head; the stones keep the shallow bright patch where the stroke stopped, and neither man names the other's silence. The Seed 22 half-check returns after a hundred and fifty days and comes changed --- in the same breath as a finished sentence and a waiting finger, with both men looking elsewhere --- so that the equality under the roof moves a third time, held and unspoken, not a reconciliation, not a hearing, not a payment, no slate entered and the loan still uncalled (T036/T076, T062). The boy files this movement on a place of its own beside the Day 161 fraction at the damper and the Day 166 held beat beneath the loaf shelf, and refuses to let three fragments stand up and call themselves a rule, for a rule is an account that has found a payer and no payer stands to any of the three (T061/T082, T100 kept apart). Tarn sweeps over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector, without once turning along it, and no collector comes; six are counted where the house can check and the seventh held where it cannot, the knife at the very edge of its sill, the Seed 16 breath unspent, nine stoppings still nine with no tenth stood up before the seventh year is earned (T036/T076, T061/T082). Through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings and never invented to stand up as a seventh; the damper's double bite is read once more as one piece of iron holding and taking, filed as an object joined to no kiln with no Grathic word for both mercies, and the two shut-room tellings stay beside it with no third.

scenes.title: Three Places and No Rule
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 171, midday into the going of the light at the yard well, the loaf shelf and under the Vail roof; no new dated heading, the day opened in Scene 3. At the well a neighbour asks what the firing will cost now the kilns are hot and is given the weather and the pot and no figure; another calls the morning a cold, and the argument ends where such arguments end, in weather (T077). From the basket's low angle at the loaf shelf the charcoal marks wait under the front edge and the boy does not read, count or copy them; Sella moves her lips along the row with its two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, and her finger does not go beneath the board this day, so the Day 166 held beat stays where it was left, a change held and unspoken and not a repeated gesture (T100 carried, not paid). The stiff brown-edged crust stays two inches from his ear, gone leathery in the dry heat, with its empty place unnamed and no third; the two shelf gaps in one room and the fold's crust and its gap in another stay apart, the shallow pan's gone place keeps its round ring on a tray of its own, the field's empty place where a hand went in on Seed 15 is gone around with a look and no number, and no third gap comes, no fourth likeness is made a cause and no finger of his draws the line (T060/T086, T097, T098 carried). He turns out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel and finds it exact and worthless: six hearings of the full note beside and never among, five from four sources and the sixth, the small flat knock out of a person as the men lifted, with no seventh and none invented; three near-full answers on their own tray, advanced and not paid, with Jorra's withheld knowing among them and not among the hearings; the older intervals at Stone 13, Stone 17 and Stone 25 with the half-beat behind a standing finger and the stroke that went on over the flagstones without the check; and nine stoppings of the near-saying as objects and not a rule, intervals and not payments, no payer named to any, with no tenth stood up and the seventh year not given (T061/T082, T036/T076). The morning's third movement of the equality goes on a place of its own beside the Day 161 fraction at the damper and the Day 166 held beat beneath the shelf --- three held changes and not a pair or a doctrine --- and the told bell stays beside the heard bell with the kiln's missing fifth and the boards' knot in three places that do not become one (T062, T100, T036/T076). Sella glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and does not touch it; she tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, counts under her breath toward no opening, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not look toward the bed (T058/T079). The fire answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and seventy-one days (T088), and the boy is one hundred and seventy-one days old and nobody says so (T071/T072). At the going of the light she sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face and leaves the thread frozen; the widow's mark is untouched because a dusk is not an opening, the two rooms do not touch, and the charcoal under the shelf waits for a hand that is not his and a day that has not come.

scenes.title: Six Counted, the Next I Don't Count
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, third dated heading: Day 172, Tallow 23, Thirdday, morning through the afternoon at the Clay Yard, the yard well and the kindling under the Vail roof. The firing month's last tend is in its third day with the kilns at their heat; the danger gathers in the dust ground small as meal, the sweetish lead edge on a wrong wind and the kiln's breath in fours with a gap, and no room is changed and no pot lost. Tarn takes the broom only after it has been given its instruction and tells the kindling Six counted. The next I don't count, with the small knife at the very edge of its sill, six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh held at the lip of the sill where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it (T036/T076). His chest has been tight since the dark, Ash is worked into the creases of his knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and no scrubbing lifts it, the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holds what light there is and gives it back, and the warm stone Sella gave him in the winter Garl died lies cold in the clay pot in the loft, two years gone and unreconciled with the debt by not trying, which is not forgiving (T006 held). He says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late, agrees so entirely that no argument can find a foot, and goes on wanting the late because a late thaw puts off the paying, though the paying has stood in the ruts since the water went; his broom goes over the collector's road without once turning along it and no collector comes. The sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it comes to his teeth and no further: he draws the breath he should have spent, does not say the word that would call the loan, does not spend the Seed 16 breath, and does not stand a tenth stopping up to join the nine, because the seventh year has not yet been earned; the near-saying stays where it has stayed and the loan stays uncalled (T036/T076, T061/T082). At the well a woman asks what the kilns will want now the last week is in and is given the weather, the pot and the river, never a figure; the yard goes around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). Sella tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes a strand of coal-black hair back with the wrist that carries the little-door burn so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not touch the widow's mark, because a morning and a shelf are not openings (T058/T079). The surgeon's register reads the held breath as a clamp left too long and the near-saying stopped at the word as a chart closed over its finding with the neat margin showing: the reading of the cold vessel and the held word is exact and worth nothing at two paces. The carried fire under the broken pot answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and seventy-two days (T088), and the boy's count stands at one hundred and seventy-two, exact, complete and unspent, spoken by nobody under any roof (T071/T072). The old life stays offstage, no tagged memory and no Chicago break (T004).

scenes.title: A List of Instruments
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 172, Tallow 23, Thirdday, the going of the light down the clay road and the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof. At the going of the light Sella carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke going before her and the river wind coming up to meet it, going wide around the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough and the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie, and gives no explanation of the turns to the basket; she sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without once looking at his face, leaves the thread of drool frozen and unwiped because nobody under any roof has been given an instruction about the thread, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed before it goes away, tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, stands a moment counting under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist, sets the pot rim out with its handle standing two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not look toward the bed. The widow's mark hangs where it hung and is not touched, because a dusk is not an opening and the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour (T058/T079). In the small hours he turns out the file the way a man lays instruments on a towel before a case begins, each thing going into its own hollow and nothing resting across anything else. Six hearings of the full note lie beside and never among, five from four sources and the sixth, the small flat knock out of a woman as the men lifted, from a person, with no seventh and none invented to fill the empty place; three near-full answers stand on their own tray, advanced and not paid, with the wheel-keeper's withheld knowing among them and not among the hearings; the older intervals lie at Stone 13, Stone 17 and Stone 25 with the half-beat behind a standing finger and the stroke that went on over the flagstones without the check; and on the widened tray nine stoppings of the near-saying stand as objects and not a rule, intervals and not payments, no payer named to any, with a tenth that has not stood up out of the nine and a seventh year that has not given (T061/T082, T036/T076). The damper lies beside them as one iron with two bites joined to no kiln, the bite that holds a vessel whole and the bite that can take the hand off a man, with no word in Grathic that would hold both mercies in one mouthful (T062). The Day 161 fraction at the damper, the Day 166 held beat beneath the loaf shelf and the third movement of the equality on Tallow 22 stand on three separate places, three held changes and not a pair or a doctrine, with no payer named to any and no word spoken over any of them (T062, T100, T036/T076). The two shut-room tellings stand side by side with no third (T065/T095), and the told bell stands beside the heard bell, four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself (T078 carried). In the other room the one stiff brown-edged crust lies two inches from his ear, gone leathery, with its empty place beside it still unnamed and no third; the loaf shelf keeps its two unnamed gaps and the charcoal waits under its front edge for a hand that is not his and a day that has not come; the shallow pan's gone place keeps the round shape of its absence on a tray of its own, the field's empty place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out stays where the yard went around it, and the sixth green is a colour joined to no ear and the foundling a shape with no sale (T060/T086, T097, T098, T050/T051 held offstage). No third gap comes, no fourth likeness is made a cause and no finger of his draws the line. Through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings and never invented to stand up as a seventh; through the floor the carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been; overhead the boards keep four nails, four and a knot the width of a thumb. Three counts in three places, and none of them rises up and becomes the others. Cold arrives in its known order, cheek, temple, the small bare joint at the wrist where the wool rides back, and stops there as if it had reached the end of its instruction. He wants the crust, the breast, the pot handle two inches beyond his hand and the number spoken by somebody who would have known what a number was, and gets none of them; he has stopped expecting to be told what the number counts, which is not the same as not wanting it. One hundred and seventy-two stands exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool, spoken by nobody under any roof (T071/T072). His hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water and comes down against the fold. The payer under the floor has had no name for a hundred and seventy-two days (T088), and the charcoal waits under the shelf for a hand that is not his and a day that has not come. Nothing is joined, paid, named, opened, called, spent or ended; the last tend of Tallow stands three days from its Account-day and the month goes out without a boundary drawn, and the count goes forward into Day 173.
